items.title: Roy Carew Interview, 1961-06-21
items.q: the boy I practiced with that was going to be my partner, he stuck to it and he became one of the best in the country.

ctx.x: All right. That, that, that gives a pretty good background as, as to, uh, how you, uh, happened to notice the music that you were listening to. Now, uh, certainly, uh, people like Sushan tell the story from the standpoint of a participant. And apparently he was alert to, uh, the changes that were occurring from, uh, year to year in those early years. And I, I think that, uh, your stories might very well corroborate the many things he tells. Uh, you mentioned baby seals in vaudeville. Uh, there were an awful lot…

The minstrel show was a very popular thing at that time. And for a number of years after that, I don't know when it began to fade, maybe in the early twenties, I don't know, or the late, uh, 19s. But, uh, but, uh, at that time, minstrel shows were a big thing. And, uh, they, they, you've got some very good talent in minstrel shows. All good talent of all kinds. They didn't stand strictly on Negro stuff. But, uh, there were, there would be acrobatics and, uh, singers of other types there, you know, different acts,…

Well, uh, you, you heard Kennedy. Now, you, uh, also heard the street bands. Did, did you think that in these first years, 1904, 1905, or six, that you also heard theatrical, uh, music that might relate to the ragtime and the jazz sequence of events?
